chapter.name: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

questions.q: The stage of human life that comes between childhood and adulthood is called:
questions.a: Adolescence. The chapter lists the stages as infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age, so adolescence lies between childhood and adulthood.

questions.q: Acne is common during adolescence mainly because:
o: oily secretions from the skin increase and can clog the skin pores
the voice box grows larger and presses on the skin
the body stops gaining height and weight
hair begins to grow in the armpits
questions.a: Oily secretions from the skin increase during adolescence; they can clog the skin pores and lead to infections, which shows up as small reddish pimples.

questions.q: Dhruv is 11. His doctor tells his parents that the increase in height becomes more prominent during adolescence. Which prediction about Dhruv agrees best with the chapter?
o: His height may increase faster in the next few years, though the timing differs from person to person
His height will stop increasing once he turns 12
He will grow by exactly the same amount every year until he is 19
His body only started growing taller after he turned 10
questions.a: His height may increase faster in the next few years, but the timing varies. The chapter says height increases from birth, becomes more prominent in adolescence, and the timing and extent of changes vary among individuals.

questions.q: Match each observation in Column I with the explanation from the chapter in Column II. Column I: 1. At 15, Rohan's old school shirts still fit in length but feel tight across the shoulders and chest.  2. Kiran, 13, has fine dark hair on his upper lip, and his uncle says it will thicken over the next few years.  3. Leela, 13, and her brother Vinod, 14, both notice new hair in their armpits.  4. Meena, 13, has grown taller and gained weight, and her breasts have begun to develop. Column II: (p) boys' shoulders may become a bit broader and their chests wider as they grow  (q) facial hair in boys later grows into a moustache and a beard  (r) hair grows in the armpits and pubic region in both boys and girls  (s) girls also undergo changes in height and weight, and other body changes like development of breasts.
questions.a: 1-p, 2-q, 3-r, 4-s: tight shirts across the shoulders and chest show broader shoulders and a wider chest; hair on the upper lip is facial hair that later grows into a moustache and beard; armpit hair appears in both boys and girls; girls also change in height and weight and develop breasts.

questions.q: Assertion (A): At 14, Jaya's voice has changed only slightly, while her twin brother Jai's voice has become hoarse. Reason (R): The voice box grows in adolescent girls too, but it does not become as big as in boys. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both are true and R explains A: the voice box grows in both, but it grows bigger in boys, so the boy's voice turns hoarse while the girl's changes only slightly.

questions.q: True or False: Humans, like most other living beings, cannot reproduce immediately after birth. Give the verdict and the reason.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: the body must first grow and reach a stage of maturity before it can reproduce
questions.a: True. Like a seedling that cannot produce seeds at once, a human body must grow and reach maturity before it is able to reproduce.

questions.q: Name the five stages of the journey of human life given in the chapter, in the correct order.
s: Names all five stages: infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age
Writes them in the correct order from infancy to old age
questions.a: Infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age.

questions.q: (a) What is acne? (b) On which part of the body are pimples commonly visible? (c) How are acne and pimples related?
s: (a) A skin condition in which small, reddish pimples appear
(b) On the face
(c) Acne is the condition; pimples are a manifestation of it
questions.a: (a) Acne is a skin condition in which small, reddish pimples appear. (b) Pimples are commonly visible on the face. (c) Acne is the condition and pimples are how it shows (a manifestation of it).

questions.q: At a family function in Guntur, 70-year-old Grandfather Rao looks at his four grandchildren: Sameer, aged 6 months; Lata, aged 8; Kunal, aged 14; and Priya, aged 25. Kunal's voice has become hoarse, a small bump can now be seen in the front of his throat, and he has grown 8 cm taller in one year. Lata says that so far she has only grown in height and weight. (a) Name the stage of life of Sameer and of Priya. (b) Which grandchild is in adolescence? (c) What is the bump in Kunal's throat called? (d) Why has Kunal's voice become hoarse?
s: (a) Sameer: infancy; Priya: adulthood
(b) Kunal, aged 14, within the 10-19 range
(c) Adam's apple
(d) His voice box has grown during adolescence
questions.a: (a) Sameer, a baby of 6 months, is in infancy and Priya in adulthood. (b) Kunal, aged 14, is in adolescence (about 10-19 years). (c) The bump is the Adam's apple. (d) In adolescent boys the voice box grows, which makes the voice sound hoarse.

questions.q: A poster in a school corridor says: "1. Every boy gets an Adam's apple, a moustache and chest hair by 13. 2. Your height stops increasing at 12. 3. Pimples mean you do not wash your face." Evaluate each of the three claims using the chapter, state the general point the poster misses, and rewrite it as two correct lines.
s: Claim 1 is wrong: the Adam's apple is not noticeable in every individual and a few boys have no significant hair growth; timing varies
Claim 2 is wrong: height increases from birth and the increase becomes more prominent during adolescence (about 10-19 years)
Claim 3 is wrong: acne comes from increased oily secretions of the skin clogging pores during adolescence
General point: the timing, nature and extent of changes vary among individuals and these variations are normal
Two correct replacement lines consistent with the chapter
questions.a: All three claims are wrong. 1: the Adam's apple is not noticeable in everyone and some boys have little hair growth. 2: height keeps increasing and the increase is most prominent in adolescence. 3: acne is caused by extra oily secretions clogging pores. The poster misses that the timing, nature and extent of changes vary and are normal. Possible lines: "Everyone changes at their own pace during adolescence." "Pimples come from extra oil in the skin; keep the skin clean."

questions.q: Changes such as a change in voice in boys and the development of breasts in girls are not directly involved in reproduction but help distinguish males from females. They are called:
questions.a: Secondary sexual characteristics: features that help distinguish males from females but are not directly involved in reproduction.

questions.q: Rahul, 13, tells his class, "Puberty means only the changes we can see from outside, like my new moustache." Which reply agrees with the chapter?
o: He is wrong: puberty includes both external and internal changes, such as the maturation of parts involved in reproduction, that make the body capable of reproduction
He is right: internal changes begin only after puberty has ended
He is right: a moustache is directly involved in reproduction, so it is all puberty needs
He is wrong: puberty includes only internal changes, so a moustache has nothing to do with it
questions.a: Rahul is wrong. Puberty is the stage in which the body undergoes external and internal changes to develop into an adult capable of reproduction; internal changes such as the maturation of parts involved in reproduction are not visible from outside, while a moustache is a secondary sexual characteristic that marks the onset of puberty.

questions.q: Read the statements. Statement I: The menstrual cycle is one of the signs of good reproductive health. Statement II: Usually, by the age of 45-55, menstruation stops naturally. Statement III: A healthy girl's menstrual cycle always lasts exactly 28 days. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: Statements I and II are correct. Statement III is wrong: the cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days, and many healthy girls have longer or shorter cycles ranging from 21 to 35 days.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The growth of facial hair in boys is a secondary sexual characteristic. Reason (R): Secondary sexual characteristics are directly involved in the process of reproduction. Choose the correct option.
o: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: A is true but R is false. Facial hair is a secondary sexual characteristic, but such characteristics are NOT directly involved in reproduction; they only help distinguish males from females.

questions.q: True or False: Menstruation, the phase of the menstrual cycle when blood discharge occurs, may last for three to seven days. Give the verdict and the reason.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: the chapter states that the phase of blood discharge, menstruation, may last three to seven days
questions.a: True. The chapter says the phase of the cycle in which blood discharge occurs is called menstruation and it may last for three to seven days.

questions.q: (a) Define puberty. (b) Name one internal change that happens during puberty.
s: (a) The stage in which the body of an adolescent undergoes external and internal changes to develop into an adult capable of reproduction
(b) Maturation of the parts involved in reproduction, or the onset of the menstrual cycle in girls
questions.a: (a) Puberty is the stage in which an adolescent's body undergoes external and internal changes to become an adult capable of reproduction. (b) The parts involved in reproduction mature (in girls the menstrual cycle begins).

questions.q: Ravi says, "Secondary sexual characteristics are useless, because they play no part in reproduction." (a) What use does the chapter give for them? (b) What do they signal about the body?
s: (a) They help distinguish males from females
(b) They are natural signs that the body is preparing for adulthood and mark the onset of puberty
questions.a: (a) Although not directly involved in reproduction, they help distinguish males from females. (b) They are natural signs that the body is preparing for adulthood and they mark the onset of puberty, so Ravi is wrong to call them useless.

questions.q: For each change, say whether it can be seen from outside or is internal, and whether it is a secondary sexual characteristic: (i) growth of chest hair in boys, (ii) maturation of the parts involved in reproduction, (iii) development of breasts in girls.
s: (i) Observable from outside; a secondary sexual characteristic
(ii) Internal, not visible from outside; not a secondary sexual characteristic (it is directly linked to reproduction)
(iii) Observable from outside; a secondary sexual characteristic
questions.a: (i) Chest hair is observable and is a secondary sexual characteristic. (ii) Maturation of reproductive parts is an internal change that cannot be seen and is directly involved in reproduction, so it is not a secondary sexual characteristic. (iii) Development of breasts is observable and is a secondary sexual characteristic.

questions.q: Anu, 11, has heard two things from neighbours: "A girl must stay away from the family during her periods" and "If you feel pain in your lower abdomen during your period, something is wrong with your body." Evaluate both claims for Anu using the chapter, and tell her one fact about when menstruation ends and one way society can help.
s: First claim judged wrong: physical isolation is a myth; menstruation is a natural process and such myths have no scientific basis
Second claim judged wrong: the chapter says some girls may feel pain or discomfort in the lower abdomen during these days, so such pain alone does not mean something is wrong
Menstruation usually stops naturally by the age of 45-55
A scientific outlook towards menstruation helps society promote good reproductive health of women
questions.a: Both claims are wrong. Isolation during periods is a myth with no scientific basis, because menstruation is a natural process. Some girls may feel pain or discomfort in the lower abdomen during menstruation, so the pain alone does not mean something is wrong. Menstruation usually stops naturally by 45-55. Encouraging a scientific outlook helps society promote good reproductive health of women.

questions.q: A health volunteer in a village school in Odisha asked 40 girls of Classes 7 and 8 one question about their last period, and each girl ticked one answer. 14 girls ticked "I was made to sit in a separate room", 10 ticked "I missed at least one day of school", and 16 ticked "Nothing changed in my routine". Several girls also said they felt ashamed. (a) What percentage of the girls were made to sit apart? (b) What is the phase of the cycle with blood discharge called? (c) Is keeping girls apart supported by science? Give the chapter's reason. (d) The school can run only one programme this term: a talk for parents on myths about menstruation, or a prize for full attendance. Which should it choose? Justify using the data.
s: (b) Menstruation
(c) No; menstruation is a natural process and isolation is a myth with no scientific basis
(d) The talk for parents: the largest problem group (35%) is isolation, which comes from a myth, and shame comes from myths, which an attendance prize does not address
questions.a: (a) 14 out of 40 = 35%. (b) Menstruation. (c) No. Menstruation is a natural process; physical isolation is a myth with no scientific basis. (d) The talk for parents: 35% of girls were made to sit apart and others felt ashamed, both caused by myths that families hold; a prize for attendance does not remove the myths that cause them.

questions.q: Which of these is listed in the chapter as a key emotional change in adolescence?
questions.a: Mood swings. The other three are physical changes or body functions, not emotional changes.

questions.q: Which of these is suggested in the chapter as a way for positive growth and development during adolescence?
o: Engaging in varied activities like music, dance or sports
Keeping all feelings hidden from everyone
Avoiding any new interest or hobby
questions.a: Engaging in varied activities like music, dance or sports is one of the ways for positive growth listed in Table 6.2.

questions.q: Ananya, 13, often feels restless. She starts designing small toys from waste cardboard and later wins a prize for an original design. In the chapter's Table 6.2, her new activity best matches which way for positive growth?
o: Self-exploration and involvement in activities that may lead to creativity and innovation
Compassion and involvement in social work
A key emotional change called increased sensitivity
questions.a: Self-exploration and involvement in activities that may lead to creativity and innovation: she explored a new interest and produced an original design.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Adolescence is often marked by stronger emotions than childhood. Reason (R): Some adolescents develop a deeper interest in new areas. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both are true, but R does not explain A. A deeper interest in new areas is an effect of the stronger emotions on behaviour, not the reason why emotions are stronger.

questions.q: (a) Name two key emotional changes in adolescents listed in the chapter. (b) Name one way for positive growth and development.
s: (a) Any two of: mood swings, strong emotions, increased sensitivity
(b) Any one of: varied activities like music, dance or sports; self-exploration and creative activities; compassion and social work
questions.a: (a) Mood swings, strong emotions or increased sensitivity (any two). (b) For example, engaging in music, dance or sports.

questions.q: Farhan, 14, is in the school dance group. These days he feels cheerful and full of energy in the morning but gloomy and irritated by evening, for no clear reason. A friend tells him to leave the dance group until his moods settle. (a) Name this emotional change. (b) Is leaving the dance group a wise step? Decide, using Table 6.2 and the chapter's line about understanding emotions.
s: (a) Mood swings

(b) Not wise: Table 6.2 suggests engaging in varied activities like music, dance or sports for positive growth, and understanding how emotions influence behaviour helps him respond thoughtfully instead of giving up the activity
questions.a: (a) Mood swings. (b) No. Table 6.2 lists engaging in varied activities like music, dance or sports as a way for positive growth during such emotional changes, so dance helps him; understanding how his emotions influence his behaviour will help him make better choices rather than quit.

questions.q: (a) How do the emotions of adolescents compare with those of children, according to the chapter? (b) Give one helpful way in which strong emotions may affect an adolescent's behaviour. (c) Why is it useful to understand how emotions influence behaviour?
s: (a) Adolescence is often marked by stronger emotions than childhood
(b) Joining social initiatives to support the needy and disadvantaged, or developing deeper interest in new areas
(c) It helps us make better choices and respond to situations thoughtfully
questions.a: (a) Adolescents often have stronger emotions than children. (b) They may join social initiatives to help the needy or develop a deeper interest in new areas. (c) Understanding it helps them make better choices and respond thoughtfully.

questions.q: A parent says, "My 13-year-old has mood swings, so he must be ill and should only see a doctor." Analyse this claim using the chapter: is it right, what explains mood swings at this age, and what does the chapter suggest instead?
s: Verdict: the claim is not right; mood swings are a key emotional change of normal adolescence
Explanation: many adolescent changes are due to hormones, and some hormones influence mood and behaviour
Suggestion: varied activities (music, dance, sports), creative activities or social work, and understanding emotions to make better choices
questions.a: The claim is not right. Mood swings are listed as a key emotional change of adolescence, which is a normal stage. Some hormones produced in the body influence mood and behaviour. Instead of treating it as illness, the chapter suggests activities like music, dance, sports, creative work or social work, and understanding how emotions affect behaviour.

questions.q: Your school wants to start an 'Adolescent Wellness Club' for Class 7 students. Using Table 6.2 of the chapter, propose four club activities. For each activity, name the emotional change or effect on behaviour it responds to, and the way for positive growth it uses.
s: Activity 1 linked to an emotional change (e.g. sports or dance for mood swings) and to varied activities
Activity 2 linked to self-exploration and creativity/innovation (e.g. a craft or science project)
Activity 3 linked to compassion and social work (e.g. helping the needy), drawing on the effect of joining social initiatives
Activity 4 that helps students understand how emotions influence behaviour (e.g. a discussion circle), linked to making better choices
questions.a: Example: (1) a music, dance or sports hour for students with mood swings or strong emotions; (2) a maker corner for self-exploration that may lead to creativity and innovation; (3) a monthly drive to support the needy, using compassion and social work; (4) a talk circle where students discuss how their emotions affect their actions, so they can respond thoughtfully.

questions.q: A school counsellor in Mysuru asked four Class 7 students to note, out of 6 school days, on how many days they felt low. In week 1 none of them took part in any activity. In week 2 Asha joined the dance group, Babu helped at a food collection for a shelter for the needy, Chitra built a model for the science fair, and Dev joined nothing. Days felt low (week 1, week 2): Asha 4, 1; Babu 5, 2; Chitra 3, 1; Dev 4, 4. (a) Find the total number of low days of Asha, Babu and Chitra together in week 1 and in week 2. (b) Name the way for positive growth from Table 6.2 that each of Asha, Babu and Chitra followed. (c) Feeling energetic on some days and low on others is which key emotional change? (d) Dev's parents say the activities are a waste of study time and the others improved only by chance. Evaluate their view, using the data and the chapter.
s: (a) Week 1: 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 days; week 2: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 days
(b) Asha: varied activities like music, dance or sports; Babu: compassion and social work; Chitra: self-exploration and creativity or innovation
(c) Mood swings
(d) Data: the three who joined fell from 12 to 4 low days, while Dev, who joined nothing, stayed at 4 and 4

(d) Chapter: these activities are the ways for positive growth listed in Table 6.2, and understanding and channelling emotions helps make better choices; so the view is not supported, though four students is a small group to be sure
questions.a: (a) Week 1: 12 low days; week 2: 4 low days. (b) Asha: varied activities like dance; Babu: compassion and social work; Chitra: self-exploration leading to creativity and innovation. (c) Mood swings. (d) The view is not supported. The three who joined an activity went from 12 to 4 low days, while Dev, who joined nothing, stayed at 4; and the chapter lists these activities as ways for positive growth during a stage of strong emotions. A group of four is small, so the school could check with more students, but cancelling the activities is not justified.

questions.q: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs are good sources of a nutrient that helps in the formation of blood. Which nutrient is it?
questions.a: Iron. Table 6.3 lists spinach, kidney beans and dried fruits like raisins and figs as sources of iron, which helps in the formation of blood.

questions.q: Which scientist studied the structure of vitamin B12 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1964?
questions.a: Dorothy Hodgkin studied the structure of vitamin B12 and in 1964 became the third woman to win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

questions.q: An adolescent girl in a rural area of Bihar needs sanitary pads free of charge or at a reduced price, and her village would also like awareness programmes on menstrual hygiene. Which initiative described in the chapter is meant for exactly this?
questions.a: The Menstrual Hygiene Scheme provides pads free or at a reduced price to adolescent girls in rural areas and runs awareness programmes. RKSK works through peer education, Shuchi is a Karnataka scheme, and Nasha Mukt Bharat is about substance abuse.

questions.q: Read the statements. Statement I: Ritu washes her armpits and pubic region well every day; this may protect her from potential infections. Statement II: A girl who wraps a used sanitary pad in newspaper and puts it inside a dustbin is helping community health and environmental cleanliness. Statement III: A school that buys biodegradable sanitary pads is choosing an environment-friendly product. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: All three are correct: hygiene of the armpits and pubic region may protect from potential infections; wrapping used pads in newspaper and disposing of them inside a dustbin ensures community health and environmental cleanliness; biodegradable sanitary pads are environment-friendly.

questions.q: Match each initiative in Column I with its feature in Column II. Column I: 1. Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram  2. Suvidha Sanitary Napkin Initiative  3. Shuchi Scheme  4. Menstrual Hygiene Scheme. Column II: (p) biodegradable pads at affordable prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras  (q) encourages peer education, where older students help younger ones  (r) a state-level programme of Karnataka  (s) free or reduced-price pads for adolescent girls in rural areas.
questions.a: 1-q, 2-p, 3-r, 4-s: RKSK uses peer education; Suvidha sells biodegradable pads at Jan Aushadhi Kendras; Shuchi is Karnataka's scheme; MHS gives free or reduced-price pads to rural girls.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Vitamin B12 has to be obtained from the food we eat. Reason (R): Like most vitamins, vitamin B12 cannot be made in the human body. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both are true and R explains A: because the body cannot make vitamin B12, it must come from food.

questions.q: True or False: Calcium from milk, curd and paneer helps in the formation of blood. Give the verdict and the corrected statement.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: calcium helps optimal bone growth; iron (from spinach, kidney beans, raisins, figs) helps in the formation of blood
questions.a: False. Calcium from milk, curd and paneer helps optimal bone growth. It is iron, from foods like spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs, that helps in the formation of blood.

questions.q: (a) Why is a nutritious diet of utmost importance during adolescence? (b) Besides proteins and carbohydrates, name two other kinds of nutrients adolescents need in adequate amounts.
s: (a) Adolescence is a period of growth and development marked by several changes in the body
(b) Any two of: fats, vitamins, minerals
questions.a: (a) Adolescence is a period of growth and development with many changes in the body, so a nutritious diet is very important. (b) Fats, vitamins and minerals (any two).

questions.q: Selvi, 13, trains for her school kabaddi team in Madurai and tires halfway through every practice. She says, "Rice gives me carbohydrates, so a big plate of rice before practice gives me all I need. I don't need curd or paneer." (a) Which two nutrients does the chapter say we need for proper growth and to perform well on the playground? (b) According to Table 6.3, what do proteins help the body do? (c) Is Selvi's plan enough? Give one point in its favour and one reason from the chapter why it falls short.
s: (a) Proteins and carbohydrates
(b) Proteins help proper growth, help gain strength and improve levels of energy

(c) Not enough: carbohydrates are indeed needed, but the chapter says proteins are needed too (and adequate fats, vitamins and minerals); curd and paneer are sources of proteins that help her gain strength and energy
questions.a: (a) Proteins and carbohydrates. (b) Proteins help proper growth, help gain strength and improve levels of energy. (c) Her plan is not enough. In its favour, carbohydrates are one of the nutrients needed to perform well on the playground. But the chapter says we need proteins as well, along with adequate fats, vitamins and minerals; curd and paneer are sources of proteins (and calcium and fats), and proteins are what help her gain strength and improve her energy levels.

questions.q: The girls' health committee of a Class 7 school is making a five-point checklist for its menstrual hygiene corner. Using the chapter, write: (a) two items that can be used to maintain menstrual hygiene; (b) why proper hygiene during menstruation is essential for girls; (c) what society should ensure in schools and public places; (d) an environment-friendly choice of pad; (e) what we should collectively reduce around sanitary pads.
s: (a) Sanitary pads and reusable cloth pads
(b) It is essential for both comfort and health
(c) The availability of necessary facilities to promote menstrual hygiene
(d) Biodegradable sanitary pads
(e) Any stigma around sanitary pads
questions.a: (a) Sanitary pads and reusable cloth pads. (b) For both comfort and health. (c) That the necessary facilities to promote menstrual hygiene are available in schools and public places. (d) Biodegradable sanitary pads, which are environment-friendly. (e) Any stigma around sanitary pads.

questions.q: Using digital devices such as phones or computers to harass others by sending misleading messages, spreading false rumours or sharing personal information without consent is called:
questions.a: Cyberbullying, as described in the Science and Society box on cyberbullying.

questions.q: Someone keeps posting mocking comments about Isha's photos in an online group. What does the chapter advise Isha to do?
o: Not feel scared or helpless, handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers
Delete her account and tell no one about it
Post mocking comments about the bully in return
Share the bully's personal information online
questions.a: The chapter says that if someone tries to bully you, you should not feel scared or helpless, but handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers.

questions.q: Match each habit in Column I with the benefit or purpose the chapter gives in Column II. Column I: 1. Regular exercise and physical activities  2. Being polite and respectful towards each other  3. Seeking guidance from elders and teachers  4. Being cautious when uploading a picture online. Column II: (p) keeps body and mind fit, builds stamina and boosts mood  (q) helps create a favourable and safe environment  (r) lets more experienced people help you use social media platforms positively  (s) keeps your pictures and personal information away from strangers.
questions.a: 1-p, 2-q, 3-r, 4-s: exercise keeps body and mind fit, builds stamina and boosts mood; politeness and respect create a favourable and safe environment; guidance from elders and teachers helps us use social media positively; caution when uploading pictures keeps personal information away from strangers.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Seeking guidance from elders and teachers can help adolescents use social media platforms positively. Reason (R): Online platforms help us obtain information and make connections. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both are true, but R does not explain A. R says what online platforms are useful for; A is about guidance, which helps because we sometimes use these platforms carelessly, knowingly or unknowingly.

questions.q: True or False: Regular exercise helps only the body; it has no effect on a person's mood. Give the verdict and the corrected statement.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: regular exercise keeps both body and mind fit, builds stamina and boosts mood
questions.a: False. The chapter says regular exercise and physical activities keep the body and mind fit and healthy, build stamina and boost mood.

questions.q: (a) Write two 'dos' for social media given in the chapter's Table 6.4. (b) Write the one 'don't' printed in the same table.
s: (a) Any two of: be respectful and kind; think before posting; protect privacy
(b) Do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends
questions.a: (a) Be respectful and kind; think before posting; protect privacy (any two). (b) Do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends.

questions.q: Class 7B makes an online group to share notes before exams. (a) Give two ways the group can use this platform for the collective well-being of all its members. (b) Which 'do' from Table 6.4 should a member follow before forwarding a message she has received?
s: (a) Two responsible uses, e.g. sharing correct notes and information, helping classmates, polite and kind messages
(b) Think before posting (and be respectful and kind)
questions.a: (a) For example, sharing correct notes and useful information, and helping one another politely. (b) Think before posting: she should check whether the message is true and kind before forwarding it.

questions.q: (a) Give two benefits of regular exercise named in the chapter. (b) Why should we be polite and respectful towards each other? (c) Name two ways in which a cyberbully may harass others.
s: (a) Two of: keeps body and mind fit and healthy, builds stamina, boosts mood
(b) It helps create a favourable and safe environment
(c) Two of: sending misleading messages, spreading false rumours, sharing personal information without consent
questions.a: (a) It keeps the body and mind fit and builds stamina (it also boosts mood). (b) It helps create a favourable and safe environment. (c) Sending misleading messages and spreading false rumours (or sharing personal information without consent).

questions.q: Decide which of these four online actions are cyberbullying, giving the chapter's reason in each case. (i) Nikhil makes a fake post in a classmate's name saying the classmate is leaving the cricket team because he is scared, so that others laugh at him. (ii) Priya tells the class group that the library is closed on Friday, after the librarian asked her to pass on the message. (iii) Reema sends her friend's phone number and photo to a gaming group of strangers without asking her friend. (iv) Varun tells his online followers that a new boy in class has an infectious disease, which is untrue, and people start avoiding the boy.
s: (i) Cyberbullying: a misleading message sent to harass someone
(ii) Not cyberbullying: true information shared to help, with no harassment
(iii) Cyberbullying: personal information shared without consent, and with strangers
(iv) Cyberbullying: spreading a false rumour
questions.a: (i) Yes: a misleading post made to harass. (ii) No: she passes on a true message to help others. (iii) Yes: personal information shared without consent, with strangers. (iv) Yes: a false rumour spread about someone. So (i), (iii) and (iv) are cyberbullying.

questions.q: Kavya, 13, of Vijayawada kept a 7-day log of her evenings. Minutes on social media: Mon 120, Tue 150, Wed 90, Thu 180, Fri 60, Sat 150, Sun 90. Outdoor games: 30 minutes on Tuesday and 45 minutes on Friday, none on other days. On Thursday a classmate sent Kavya misleading messages about the date of the inter-school quiz, so that she missed the selection round, and others in the class group then mocked her. (a) Find her total social-media time for the week in hours, and her daily average in minutes. (b) On how many days did she play outdoors? Give two benefits the chapter links with regular physical activity. (c) What is the classmate's act called, and what should Kavya do? (d) The class group's admins propose two changes. Plan X: remove Kavya from the group so that nobody can upset her there. Plan Y: every member agrees to 'be respectful and kind' and to 'think before posting', and the class teacher is told about the misleading messages. Which plan agrees better with the chapter? Justify.
s: (a) 120+150+90+180+60+150+90 = 840 minutes = 14 hours; average 840/7 = 120 minutes a day
(b) 2 days; two of: keeps body and mind fit and healthy, builds stamina, boosts mood
(c) Cyberbullying (misleading messages sent to harass); she should not feel scared or helpless, handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers

(d) Plan Y: the chapter asks us to be polite and respectful and use online platforms responsibly for the collective well-being of all, with the dos 'be respectful and kind' and 'think before posting', and to seek help from teachers; Plan X punishes the one who was bullied and changes nothing in the others' behaviour
questions.a: (a) 840 minutes = 14 hours; 840/7 = 120 minutes a day. (b) 2 days; regular exercise keeps the body and mind fit, builds stamina and boosts mood. (c) Cyberbullying: misleading messages sent to harass her. Kavya should not feel scared or helpless, handle it wisely and seek help from her parents and teachers. (d) Plan Y. The chapter says we should be polite and respectful, use online platforms responsibly for the collective well-being of all, follow the dos 'be respectful and kind' and 'think before posting', and seek help from teachers when someone is bullied. Plan X removes the student who was harmed while the behaviour that harmed her stays the same.

questions.q: The Government has launched a National De-addiction Helpline to deal with drug addiction and help drug addicts. Its number is:
questions.a: 14446 is the National De-addiction Helpline number given in the chapter.

questions.q: Which of these best describes hormones, as explained in the chapter?
o: Chemicals produced in our bodies that regulate growth and development
Nutrients that must be obtained only from the food we eat
Harmful substances that make people addicted
Structures in the throat that help us to speak
questions.a: Hormones are certain chemicals produced in our bodies; they regulate various aspects of growth and development.

questions.q: Read the statements. Statement I: Which health problem a harmful substance causes, such as breathing difficulties or memory loss, depends on the substance. Statement II: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan mainly aims to treat adults who are already addicted. Statement III: The National De-addiction Helpline 14446 is meant only for people who smoke. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: Only Statement I is correct: the chapter says these substances cause problems such as breathing difficulties, memory loss and lung damage, depending on the substance. Statement II is wrong: the Abhiyaan spreads awareness on avoiding substance abuse, with special focus on prevention among early-age children. Statement III is wrong: the helpline is to deal with drug addiction and help drug addicts, not only smokers.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Menstruation and other signs of puberty are mainly due to hormones. Reason (R): Hormones are chemicals produced in the body that play a crucial role in regulating growth and development. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both are true and R explains A: hormones regulate growth and development, and so they bring about the changes of puberty, including menstruation.

questions.q: (a) Name two harmful substances that peers may pressure adolescents to consume. (b) Name two health problems that such substances can cause.
s: (a) Any two of: tobacco, gutka, cigarettes, beedi, alcohol, illegal drugs
(b) Any two of: breathing difficulties, memory loss, damage to the lungs
questions.a: (a) For example, tobacco and alcohol (also gutka, cigarettes, beedi, illegal drugs). (b) For example, breathing difficulties and damage to the lungs (also memory loss).

questions.q: Gopal's uncle has chewed gutka every day for years and now wants to stop. (a) According to the chapter, what is the first step to overcoming addiction? (b) Name one other kind of help and one government service the uncle can use.
s: (a) Seeking help and support from family and friends and talking to trusted people
(b) Counselling or medical advice; the National De-addiction Helpline 14446
questions.a: (a) The first step is seeking help and support from family and friends and talking to trusted people. (b) Counselling or medical advice; and the government's National De-addiction Helpline, 14446.

questions.q: (a) What are hormones? (b) Where in the body are they produced, and when are they released? (c) Apart from growth, name one thing that some hormones influence.
s: (a) Certain chemicals produced in our bodies that regulate growth and development
(b) Produced in different parts of the body; released at an appropriate time in response to signals from the brain
(c) Mood and behaviour
questions.a: (a) Hormones are chemicals produced in our bodies that regulate growth and development. (b) They are produced in different parts of the body and released at an appropriate time in response to signals from the brain. (c) Some hormones influence mood and behaviour.

questions.q: At a wedding, 14-year-old Sana's older cousins hold out a cigarette and say, "Every teenager wants to try new things." Sana answers, "Maybe later, not today." Her cousin Imran, 17, started smoking a year ago; now he smokes every day and feels a strong urge to smoke whenever he tries to skip a day. (a) Which feature of adolescence, named in the chapter, were the cousins playing on? (b) Was Sana's answer the kind the chapter advises? Justify, and write a reply that follows the chapter. (c) Using the chapter, explain how Imran's smoking became a daily habit, and give the chapter's name for such regular use.
s: (a) Curiosity and excitement, which make adolescents likely to be influenced by people who tempt, persuade or pressure them
(b) No: 'maybe later' leaves the door open; the chapter says to remain firm and confident in the decision to say NO, the first time and every time, e.g. "No. I will not smoke, today or ever."
(c) Cigarettes are addictive: once a person starts, a strong urge to take them again and again develops, and over time the person uses them regularly; this is called substance abuse
questions.a: (a) Curiosity and excitement: because adolescence is marked by them, adolescents may be influenced by people who tempt or pressure them. (b) No. 'Maybe later' keeps the option open; the chapter asks us to stay firm and confident in saying NO, the first time and every time, for example: "No. I will not smoke, today or ever." (c) Such substances are addictive: once Imran started, he developed a strong urge to smoke again and again, and over time he began smoking regularly. The chapter calls this substance abuse.

questions.q: A school has Rs 6,000 for an anti-substance-abuse week and wants to run exactly three of these: (A) posters showing the National De-addiction Helpline, Rs 1,500; (B) a talk by a counsellor, Rs 2,500; (C) an inter-class football tournament, Rs 3,000; (D) pamphlets on the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan for parents, Rs 2,000. Find which set of three fits the budget, show your working, and evaluate whether the set is a good choice using the chapter.
s: Totals of the four possible sets: ABC 7,000; ABD 6,000; ACD 6,500; BCD 7,500
Only A, B and D fit the Rs 6,000 budget
Links A, B, D to the chapter: helpline 14446 for help, counselling for handling addiction, awareness through the Abhiyaan with community participation
Judgement: a good choice for awareness and help; the football tournament, though it promotes physical activity and fitness, must be dropped or funded another way
questions.a: The sets cost ABC = 7,000, ABD = 6,000, ACD = 6,500 and BCD = 7,500, so only A, B and D fit Rs 6,000. It is a good choice: posters spread the helpline 14446, a counsellor gives the counselling the chapter recommends, and pamphlets for parents spread awareness as the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan intends through community participation. The football tournament would promote physical activity but does not fit the budget.

questions.q: At a de-addiction awareness camp in Hubballi, a doctor shares records of 60 adults who came for help. 36 of them first used a harmful substance when they were between 10 and 19 years old, and 24 first used it at 20 or later. Of the 36, 27 said friends or peers pushed them into it and 9 tried it alone. One patient who smoked beedi for years has breathing difficulties; another who drank alcohol heavily has memory loss. (a) What percentage of the 60 first used a substance during adolescence? (b) What percentage of these 36 were pushed by peers? Name two ways the chapter says people may push someone. (c) A visitor says, "All these substances cause exactly the same harm." Correct him using the chapter. (d) The camp can fund one plan for the town's schools. Plan X: posters giving only the helpline number. Plan Y: classroom sessions where Class 6-8 students practise saying a firm NO to friends. Which plan better fits the data and the chapter? Justify.
s: (b) 27/36 x 100 = 75%; any two of: tempt, persuade, force, create pressure
(c) Wrong: the substances cause serious problems such as breathing difficulties, memory loss and damage to the lungs, depending on the substance (beedi smoke damages the lungs, Fig. 6.5)
(d) Plan Y: most began in adolescence (60%) and most of those under peer pressure (75%), so practising a firm NO before the first try attacks the main cause
(d) The chapter asks adolescents to remain firm and confident in saying NO and to avoid these substances completely, since they are addictive; a helpline helps after addiction, Plan Y prevents it
questions.a: (a) 36 of 60 = 60%. (b) 27 of 36 = 75%; people may tempt, persuade, force or create pressure on someone. (c) He is wrong: the chapter says these substances cause serious health problems such as breathing difficulties, memory loss and damage to the lungs, depending on the substance, as the two patients show. (d) Plan Y. The data show that 60% began during adolescence and 75% of them because peers pushed them, so the main cause is peer pressure on adolescents. The chapter asks them to stay firm and confident in saying NO and to avoid these addictive substances completely; practising that NO prevents the first use, while a helpline helps only after addiction has begun.
